clue.text: Primate in role, as protection against the enemy?

indicators.note: the primate sits in the role, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a part is an actor's role
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey cast in a play, perhaps acting as a defender against foes.
explanation.definitionFit: A low wall along a rampart shields defenders from enemy fire, hence protection with a question mark for the military sense.

clue.text: Joke doddery oldie heard in musical form

indicators.note: the solver is told these words are spoken, so their sound gives the entry

parts.note: a joke is a pun, and a doddery oldie is an old crock, a decrepit person

explanation.surface: A shaky old-timer cracks a joke that turns out to be in some musical style.
explanation.walkthrough: PUN + CROCK said together sound like the two-word genre; 'heard' is the homophone signal. A crock is British slang for a worn-out old person or thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The loud, fast, anti-establishment style of the late 1970s is a genre of popular music.

clue.text: See 1
Artist has left it for framing?

definitions.text: Artist has left it for framing?

indicators.note: PORT and IT are set around the artist, enclosing him like a frame

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter leaves his canvas behind, ready to go in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: something an artist leaves behind to be framed.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted likeness is the classic work an artist finishes and hands over to be hung in a frame.

clue.text: Athenian character penned by dramatist — I'm one

indicators.note: the letters are held, as in a pen, within the words dramatist, I'm and one

explanation.surface: A playwright claims to be the Athenian figure he wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' shows the letters sit within 'dramatisT I'M ONe'; the surface also hints at Shakespeare, who did write the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's misanthrope in Timon of Athens is a famous Athenian figure of the stage.

clue.text: The French going after instant sea food

indicators.note: the French article follows the word for an instant, so it comes second

parts.note: a wink is an instant, as in 'in a wink'
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people suddenly chase after something from the sea to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: This small edible sea snail is a traditional British seaside snack, picked out with a pin.

clue.text: Island is area for Greek character to occupy

indicators.note: the Greek letter takes up a place inside the other letters

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An island is a place set aside for a Greek to settle on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' tempts toward a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: This volcanic island lies in the Bay of Naples, off the Italian coast.

clue.text: Pirate out of place in part of ship, be honest

indicators.note: the jumbled pirate goes inside the part of the ship

parts.note: the keel is the spine along a ship's bottom

indicators.note: the letters of pirate are moved from where they belong, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A pirate found where he shouldn't be in the ship is told to come clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the pirate's letters is PITREA, which splits the keel after its second E.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges staying authentic and grounded, much like being truthful and genuine.

clue.text: Old comic publication seen as abrasive

parts.note: Dick Emery was a British TV comedian of the 1960s and 70s
a paper is a newspaper, a publication

explanation.surface: A vintage comic book is judged rather harsh in tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old comic' reads as an old comic book, but it is Dick Emery, a British TV comedian; 'abrasive' is a noun here, not 'harsh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets coated with a gritty mineral powder are used for smoothing or polishing surfaces, an abrasive material.

clue.text: Alloy with which Gypsy plugs opening

indicators.note: the Gypsy fills a gap in the opening, as a plug fills a hole

parts.note: a niche is an opening or recess, also a gap in a market
a Rom is a member of the Romany people

explanation.surface: A traveller blocks up a gap with some metal mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' suggests a doorway or a start, but here it is a recess.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickel and chromium together make a resistant metallic mix used in heating elements.

clue.text: Agree about journalist being taken in by star

indicators.note: the pair of pieces are absorbed within the star

parts.note: an ace is a star performer
C, from circa, means about
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer, swept up by a celebrity, gives consent.
explanation.definitionFit: To give consent to a request or demand is to assent or comply.

clue.text: Fate encountered after short embrace

indicators.note: the shortened embrace is placed before the meeting word, so that word comes after
the embrace is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a kiss is an embrace
met means encountered

explanation.surface: Destiny struck when two people met after a brief hug.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, from Turkish and Arabic, means destiny or the will of providence.

clue.text: Structural weakness of fairly big tin potty

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A rather large tin chamber pot proves to be flimsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' looks like a noun, a child's pot, but it is the anagram signal on FAIRLY BIG TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means the quality of being easily broken, a kind of fragility in a structure.

clue.text: Rent flat with floors at different heights

parts.note: rent, as a noun, is a tear or split
flat means level

explanation.surface: An apartment to let is described as being on several storeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent flat' reads as a flat to let; 'Rent' is a tear and 'flat' is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A house built in this style has storeys staggered by about half a floor.

clue.text: Dish and item of furniture that may be put on list of inventions

definitions.text: that may be put on list of inventions

parts.note: a paten is the dish holding bread at Communion
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A plate and a table, possibly worth registering as new inventions.
explanation.definitionFit: An invention that qualifies for official protection can be registered with the patent office.

clue.text: Very soft bit of apple expanded

parts.note: the middle of the word apple holds PP, the musical marking, and expanding that abbreviation gives the full Italian term

explanation.surface: A tiny piece of apple grows very soft.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters PP sit inside 'apple'; in music PP is shorthand for a very quiet passage, and 'expanded' asks for it written in full.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical direction tells players to perform extremely quietly.

clue.text: Snub in game

definitions.meaning: to put someone down or crush them
a racket sport played in a walled court

explanation.surface: A put-down delivered in the middle of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatten someone's hopes is to crush them; the racket sport is also called by this name.

clue.text: Atmosphere around sort of valley

indicators.note: turned around, the word for atmosphere reads backwards

parts.note: air means atmosphere

explanation.surface: A misty atmosphere hangs about a type of valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns AIR back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A drowned river valley, open to the sea, is a geographical term from Spanish.

clue.text: Second drink and girl's beginning amorous activity

parts.note: a noggin is a small measure of drink

indicators.note: only the first letter of the girl's word is taken

explanation.surface: Another round and a girl's arrival lead to some romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes G from 'girl's'. A noggin is a small tot of spirits; the answer is British slang for kissing.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolonged kissing and cuddling is British slang for lovers' activity.

clue.text: President once popular, having removed extremists

indicators.note: the word for popular loses its outermost letters, its extremes

parts.note: liked means popular

explanation.surface: A former leader was well loved after ousting radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having removed extremists' trims L and D from the ends of LIKED; 'extremists' reads as radicals but means outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower, US president in the 1950s, was nicknamed this, as in 'I like Ike'.

clue.text: Legal statement by Welby, maybe as a precaution

indicators.note: the legal statement stands beside the first name, after it

parts.note: Justin Welby was Archbishop of Canterbury; 'maybe' marks him as one example of the name
a case is a statement of arguments in court

explanation.surface: An archbishop makes a legal argument just to be safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places CASE beside JUSTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to guard against a possible future event, as a safeguard.

clue.text: Trendy Parisian quickly making request for company

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
vite is French for quickly

explanation.surface: A stylish Frenchman hurriedly asks for someone to join him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' reads as a business, but here means companionship.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone to come along to an event is a request for their companionship.

clue.text: Ten fools, cavorting with glee, lose all inhibitions

indicators.note: the letters leap about like dancers, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten clowns dance gleefully and shed all restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges TEN FOOLS with GLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to abandon self-control and behave freely without restraint.

clue.text: Tricky roles for one always taking second place?

indicators.note: tricky suggests something twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor handed difficult parts always ends up as runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' rearranges ROLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps finishing behind the winner is a habitual failure in contests.

clue.text: Was successful, like a reluctantly disciplined child?

definitions.meaning: past tense of the idiom for prospering after humble beginnings
a child forced to behave has been compelled into behaving well

explanation.surface: Success came, like a child forced into behaving.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means prospered in life; read literally it describes a youngster forced into obedience.

clue.text: See 24
Very little vigour when one's absorbed bacterium

indicators.note: the one is soaked up inside the other letters

parts.note: V is the little abbreviation for very
brio means vigour or verve
one, Roman numeral I; the 's means is

explanation.surface: Hardly any energy remains once a single germ takes hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed' puts I inside V BRIO, after V.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma-shaped microbe, such as the one causing cholera, belongs to this genus of bacteria.

clue.text: Musical phrase, last thing from radio station to be played

indicators.note: only the final letter of radio is taken
playing with the letters of station rearranges them

explanation.surface: A tune that is the final item a radio station broadcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last thing from' takes O from 'radio'; 'to be played' rearranges STATION to STINATO.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian term names a short musical pattern repeated persistently throughout a piece.

clue.text: We hear No 1 songs

indicators.note: the solver is told the word is spoken, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: the number one is the leader

explanation.surface: Word is that some tracks have topped the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' signals that LEADER sounds like the German word for songs.
explanation.definitionFit: German art songs for voice and piano, by Schubert and others, are known by this plural.

clue.text: Plant that's crimson gets weak in time when secluded

indicators.note: the time-and-weak group is shut away inside the colour

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red

indicators.note: weak is placed within the time word

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A crimson bloom fades while hidden away for a period.
explanation.walkthrough: The weak letter goes into the time word first, making AGWE, which then sits inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: This weed with yellow flowers, a cause of hay fever, is a wild plant.
